title: Why he left the band: Betty Hutton and the Paramount contract
summary: He left for Betty Hutton and the plan to write songs with Jack Segal, leading to contracts with Paramount and Capitol.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Why did you leave the band the first time?
She had invited you to go to the coast--I'm not sure I remember the details on that exactly.
Well, we wanted to be together and the only way to do it was for me to go out there.
On a tour. On a theater tour. We were the band and she was the
And she had to go back for her Paramount commitment?

I decided to take a crack at songwriting, she said she knew Johnny Mercer very well and she was attached to Capital Records, so if I would write some songs and send them out if they had any merit she'd show them to Johnny, which is what happened. I ran into Jack Segal and explained it to him and we sat down and started writing together. It was very easy to write together, and he and I were knocking things off one after another easily. It just seemed to come, and Johnny liked them, everybody liked them, so we were sent for.
At the same time the material was shown to Louie Lipstone who was running the Paramount music department and Louie wanted us there, so suddenly we had a contract with Paramount
Pictures and with Capitol Records in one swelled swoop, if that's the terminology; that's how I got to the coast.
